title: Thirds
summary: A 3rd spans three letters. The minor 3rd sounds dark and the major 3rd sounds bright.

steps.title: 3rd
steps.body:
Count three letters: C, D, E. C to E is a **3rd**. Like 2nds, 3rds come in a minor and a major size.

**Why it matters:** The notes a band plays together are often stacked a 3rd apart. In Unit 4 you will build them from the 3rds in this lesson.

steps.title: Minor 3rd
steps.body:
A **minor 3rd** is 3 half steps, like C to E♭ or A to C. It sounds darker.

**Why it matters:** The minor 3rd gives music its sad, dark colour. Greensleeves opens with one.

steps.title: Major 3rd
steps.body:
A **major 3rd** is 4 half steps, like C to E. It sounds brighter.

**Why it matters:** The major 3rd gives music its bright, happy colour. Oh When the Saints opens with one.

steps.title: Thirds above C
steps.body: E♭ is a minor 3rd above C, and E is a major 3rd above C.

items.prompt: Play C4, then go up a major 3rd.
Play C4, then go up a minor 3rd.
Play G4, then go up a major 3rd.
Play D4, then go up a minor 3rd.

steps.title: Slide a pair of thirds
steps.body: Hold two white keys a 3rd apart, like C and E, and slide the pair up one white key at a time. Some pairs are major 3rds and some are minor. Listen for bright and dark.

items.prompt: Play F4, then go up a major 3rd.
